title: Brevis Fidei Christianae Complexio
author: Boethius

passages.original: Haec autem ut credantur, vetus ac nova informat instructio : de qua, velut arce religionis nostræ, multi diversa, et humaniter, atque ut ita dicam, carnaliter sentientes, adversa loculi sunt: ut Arius, qui, licet Deum dicat Filium, minorem tamen Patre multipliciter et extra Patris substantiam confitetur. Sabelliani iquoque non tres existentes personas, sed unam ausi sunt affirmare : eumdem dicentesPatrernessequiFiliusest;
passages.english: That these things should be believed, the old and the new instruction teaches; concerning this [teaching], as if concerning the citadel of our religion, many who think diverse things, and in a human and, so to speak, carnal way, have spoken contrary things: such as Arius, who, although he calls the Son God, nevertheless confesses him to be in many ways less than the Father and outside the Father's substance. The Sabellians also have dared to affirm not three existing persons but one, saying that the Father is the same as the Son;
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'loculi' read as 'locuti', 'iquoque' as 'quoque', 'dicentesPatrernessequiFiliusest' as 'dicentes Patrem esse qui Filius est' (literally 'saying that he who is the Son is the Father'). 'Instructio' (old and new) refers to the Old and New Testaments.
